detailed_findings.finding: The contradiction argument correctly identifies a root of the denominator product that is not a root of the numerator product, which suffices to rule out polynomiality.

reason: The proof is mathematically sound and complete for the stated lemma. It correctly rewrites q-binomial coefficients via P_m(q), uses the symmetry [n choose r]_q = [n choose n-r]_q to reduce to a = min(k,n-k) and b = min(l,n-l), and then proves by contradiction that a < b is impossible if the quotient is polynomial. The root-of-unity argument is valid: under a < b one has b < n-a, so a primitive (n-a)-th root of unity annihilates the denominator product B(q) but not the numerator product A(q), contradicting polynomiality after cross-multiplication. This matches the lemma sketch and the role in the assembly, and no forbidden or undeclared theorem citations are used.
